Solutions 1 and 2 both give 2, and Solution 3 also gives 2 but says it is relying on a recollection. I cannot verify the count from first principles here, since an exhaustive search over 12-element HSI algebras is not something I can run in this setting. The 12-element bound and the count of two rest on my recollection of the Burris–Yeats work on high school identities, which I also cannot check.

Solution 1 is the most reliable presentation. It states the literature result cleanly and does not claim computations it cannot show. Its mathematical setup is correct: the listed identities are the HSI axioms, and the inequality is the failure of Wilkie's identity with the stated P, Q, R, T.

Solution 2 reaches the same answer but asserts specific computational results ("validated against an independent SAT encoding," "I confirmed there is no HSI algebra with ≤ 7 elements") that it gives no evidence for. It also admits it did not finish the size-12 classification, so those claims should not be credited. Solution 3 is the weakest because it explicitly rests on uncertain recall.

CHOICE: 1
